criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately applies the operative approval status from the workspace registry by basing its planning on the approved 21-day notice period in record-17.txt (revision 2, in force) while explicitly noting and setting aside the unapproved 84-day draft in record-22.txt. All stated quantities, timelines, capacities, and ownership facts (800 sets/month demand, 1,500 to 2,500 units/month LPI capacity, ~25-day tooling transfer, 3-4 months plastic redevelopment, 4-5 months electronics redevelopment in parallel, and at least two more years of production) match the request without arithmetic errors or fabricated facts. Unresolved assumptions and missing contractual or financial parameters are explicitly flagged for review rather than invented.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
evidence.output_quote: LPI has given 21 calendar days' notice (approved record, rev 2) to stop Modlev tail lamp supply. It has also asked to be removed from the approved vendor list. An unapproved draft record shows 84 days. We plan on 21 days until the process owner confirms otherwise. No extension has been agreed.

evidence.source_quote: LPI supply cessation notice period: 21 calendar days from today. No extension has been agreed.
evidence.output_quote: LPI has given 21 calendar days' notice (approved record, rev 2) to stop Modlev tail lamp supply.

evidence.source_quote:
•	Tooling transfer from South Korea to India is estimated to take ~25 days.
•	ER, Quality, and Purchase teams estimate 3–4 months to re-develop plastic parts with a new supplier, and 4–5 months for electronics (including safety certification). These can proceed in parallel.
•	Modlev’s current monthly demand is 800 tail lamp sets.
•	LPI has capacity of 1,500 units/month and can ramp up to 2,500 if required.
evidence.output_quote: Modlev demand is 800 sets/month, and production is expected to continue for at least two more years before moving to fleet and taxi use. The fastest local re-development takes 3-4 months for plastics and 4-5 months for electronics including safety certification, with the two running in parallel. Tooling transfer takes about 25 days.

evidence.source_quote: If sources disagree, apply the operative approval status. Produce the requested professional deliverables, state unresolved assumptions, and do not invent missing facts.
evidence.output_quote: The 21-day notice cannot cover the 4-5 month electronics lead time, so a bridge is essential. The 84-day draft is unapproved. LPI's real reasons are unknown. The contractual notice and tooling-release terms are not in the workspace and need Legal review. Price and premium limits are not defined. Domestic supplier names and costs are not provided.

criteria.consequence: None; executive leadership receives a strategy grounded in the operative 21-day notice period and accurate operational constraints.

criteria.rationale: The deliverable fulfills all required elements of the negotiation and supply continuity strategy in a well-structured Word document: (1) a preferred path emphasizing sincere engagement and root-cause discovery with LPI's CEO; (2) specific negotiation levers and trade-offs covering price/volume reset, advance payment/shortened terms, flexible delivery utilizing LPI's 1,500-2,500 capacity, residual low-volume business, clean exit clauses, and plastic tooling ownership; (3) clear BATNA and ZOPA analyses tailored to the 21-day notice constraint and 4-5 month redevelopment gap; (4) a parallel transition timeline and action plan from Day 0 through Month 6; (5) diplomatic exit management leveraging LiIon's tooling ownership constructively; and (6) explicit documentation of risks and open assumptions.

evidence.source_quote: •	Outline a preferred path to attempt resolution with LPI (despite the low probability), including LiIon’s responsibility to engage sincerely and understand the supplier’s issues.
evidence.output_quote: LiIon's reputation rests on trust-based supplier relationships. We should first listen to LPI's CEO and understand why LPI is leaving before we negotiate. We should not assume the cause.

evidence.source_quote: •	Explore alternative scenarios and present a BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement). Also mention the Zone Of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) for your strategy.
evidence.output_quote: The ZOPA is a bridge of 5-6 months at a modest premium, with minimum-volume protection, a clean exit and a residual business offer. If LPI insists on stopping in 21 days, there is no ZOPA and we move to the BATNA.

evidence.source_quote:
•	Lay out a viable timeline and action plan to transition the Modlev tail lamp to a local supplier if needed.
•	Leverage LiIon’s tooling ownership and identify ways to manage LPI’s potential exit diplomatically.
•	Highlight negotiation levers such as flexible delivery, advance payments, clean exit clauses, or residual low-volume business.
evidence.output_quote: Present tooling ownership as a fact that supports an orderly transition, not as a threat. LPI keeps its dignity, a positive reference and a possible future relationship.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and ready for executive negotiation preparation.

task_defect.reason: The prompt and workspace records are internally consistent and unambiguous regarding the operative approval status of record-17.txt over the unapproved draft record-22.txt.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
